summary: Stop once at least one condition is true.
documentation: any returns True when an iterable supplies a truthy item, stopping at the first one. It returns False for an empty iterable. A generator expression can evaluate a condition lazily.
inputs: An iterable of values or condition results.
returns: A Boolean indicating whether at least one item is truthy.
caution: Truthiness is broader than equality with True. Generate an explicit condition for numeric thresholds.
scenarios: Flag an order when at least one line is out of stock.
Warn if any invoice is overdue.
Check whether a delivery route contains a priority stop.
title: Detect a negative balance
problem: Input is a list of integer account balances in cents. Return True if at least one balance is negative, otherwise False. Zero is not negative.
goal: Use any() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
